summary: Repo already dissects 142 in OAI_METHOD_142.md (verdict NEGATIVE, promise 0/5: its auxiliary-prime derandomisation transfers only through bounded-index Frobenius layers, the index-2/BM layer is free, full index = B2) and HARDNESS_MAP.md A5/A6 + OAI_DUMP_IMPACT.md §2.1 (efficient ES ⇒ deterministic QNR; 003 alone already puts QNR/prime square roots in P). The concrete step: the only square-root code in the search engines (scripts/exf_engine.c:34, Type I f | p²+4c²d step) is Tonelli–Shanks with a deterministic least-QNR trial search (z=2,3,…), so no randomised step exists in practice; derandomisation is irrelevant to ES search and to existence.

Coppersmith/Lenstra/CHN 'divisors in residue classes' is analysed in BRAINSTORM/s3_lll_lenstra.md (upper bound ≤11 per Lenstra line, decision not existence, promise 0), gon_lll_relation_lattice.md (b1) and B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md row 8. I ran the item's exact step on the (★) line: the Coppersmith regime 4C ≥ (4Cp+1)^{1/4} is ⇔ uB ≲ p^{2/3}, Lenstra regime ⇔ uB ≲ p^{1/2}; among primes p≡1(4) ≤ 10^7 the Coppersmith-regime (★) sub-lottery fails at 131/293005 primes in [10^6,10^7] (0.04%; 0.2% in [10^5,10^6]; largest 9820897), Lenstra-regime fails at 0.47% — consistent with a θ² share of the (log p)² main term. Algorithmically the regime still spans ≍p^{2/3} values of C, so no polylog search and no existence mechanism; new only as a per-prime calibration of s3's per-certificate split.

Verified erdosproblems.com/298 = Bloom's theorem (positive upper density A ⇒ finite S ⊂ A with Σ1/n = 1). The repo already locates the density→pointwise gap: BRAINSTORM/addcomb_unit_fraction_density.md §3.1 (PROVED from Bloom's Prop 1: |S| ≥ N^{1−1/loglogN}/z, because the Fourier step needs many elements divisible by each prime power q | lcm(S) to equidistribute q-adically — impossible with 3 terms; §3.2 the k=3 local-cancellation shadow is exactly ET's parametrisation), z31_unit_fractions.md (c) (blocked by fixed target + 3 terms + polylog count), B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md §4.4 (ANALOGUE, NOT SHARP). The 'missing uniform lower bound' asked for is the term-count/equidistribution hypothesis, already identified.

Freedom quantified: (★) has 3 parameters (u,B,C), 1 equation, ≍(p/4)log p candidates of which ≍(3/(2π²))(log p)² succeed (FRONTIER §2.1–2.2) — free choice yields only polylog winners, whereas the proved side of the pair (a primitive root exists) rests on cyclicity with an exact positive count φ(p−1) ≍ p/loglog p. So the minimal pair is mis-aligned: ES's 'free base' is like the least-primitive-root problem in a polylog window (polylog only under GRH, Shoup), not like existence of a primitive root. This is already the repo's mechanism table B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md M1a/M2/M3/M4 (fixed-modulus character events, group action, freedom-of-choice) and z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md rows 14–15 (least primitive root, Heath-Brown).

PROVED (one line, ultrametric): if v_ℓ(n) − v_ℓ(4) = k ≥ 1 then some denominator has v_ℓ ≥ k, since v_ℓ(Σ1/x_i) ≥ min v_ℓ(1/x_i); gives v₂(n)≥4 ⇒ 4|, v₂(n)≥5 ⇒ 8|, v₃(n)≥2 ⇒ 9|, 5|n ⇒ 5| — the necessity half of every observed failure set, trivially. For odd n the 2-adic count forces exactly two denominators ≡2 (4) and one odd; inside (★) this is C odd, v₂(uB)=1, and that sub-family alone fails at 513/34392 primes p≡1(4) in [10^5,10^6] (1.5%), so the variant data's 0 prime failures ≤10^5 use non-(★) solutions. The 'exactly' (sufficiency) half is a strengthened ES conjecture (EVIDENCE only), a positive-density sub-lottery with no new leverage.

Did the step at the smallest CM discriminants: on the Type I slice of level d, f | p²+4c²d = N(p+2c√−d) with f ≡ −p (mod 4cd) gives χ_{−4d}(f)=+1 (all prime factors split/ramify) and χ_{−4d}(f)=χ_{−4d}(−p)=−χ_{−4d}(p), so the slice is non-empty only if χ_{−4d}(p)=−1 (PROVED, elementary). Hence the 'simplest' CM specialisations are exactly the dead ones: d=1 (ℤ[i]) is empty for every p≡1(4), and d=1,2,3 are all empty at the Mordell-hard p≡1(24); the live levels are those where p is inert, i.e. the least-QNR problem. This is already (I)7 / gon_fermat_certificates.md, s8_signed_genus_wall.md Lemma 4.1, markoff_hasse_failures_vs_es.md, and the CM dictionaries in cayley_markoff_cm.md, s5_cm_frobenius.md, z9_heegner_layers.md; no special-value simplification appears.

Wrote the two-part Sylvester wave explicitly (Popoviciu: p_{u,B}(n) = n/(uB) − {B′n/u} − {u′n/B} + 1) and checked: both periodic waves are extreme at n ⟺ n ≡ −(u+B) (mod uB), and then p_{u,B}(n) = (n+u+B)/(uB) − 1, so (★) at (u,B) ⟺ waves extreme at p and p_{u,B}(p) ≡ 3 (mod 4); script reproduces R(p) exactly at 7 primes incl. 409 (R=0), 2521, and Popoviciu matches brute force for uB ≤ 60. Expanding the waves in roots of unity gives R(p) = Σ_{(u,B)} (4uB)^{-1} Σ_k e(k(p+u+B)/4uB), i.e. precisely the additive/Dirichlet-character expansion already in the repo (PARITY_AUDIT Lemma 2.1 M+E, FRONTIER §2.1 genus split M_gen + X, METAPLECTIC_ES theta form). The wave language adds no new sum and no positivity; Frobenius/Popoviciu vocabulary exists only in z52b generation headers (signature_header, free_opus 0394).

Read the arXiv:2504.10992 abstract (Q.-D. Dao, 'Rational and integral points on Markoff-type K3 surfaces'): the family has Zariski-dense rational points but fails the integral Hasse principle *due to the Brauer–Manin obstruction*. That mechanism provably cannot occur for ES: U_n is everywhere locally integrally soluble and has no BM obstruction at any n ≥ 2 (Bright–Loughran, FRONTIER §1), so 'testing the analogues of their local verification on ES mod small prime powers' is vacuous — every local test passes for every n. The repo already covers Markoff/Ghosh–Sarnak failures, including the non-BM descent failures and Dao's earlier paper (arXiv:2202.07142), in MARKOFF_ES.md §§ (l.46, l.301) and BRAINSTORM/markoff_hasse_failures_vs_es.md, and the general 'local ≠ global' caution in DISPROOF_AVENUES.md l.18–58; 2504.10992 itself is cited only in z52b lanes. Note: a grep also surfaced one line of a z52b_pass1 memo on the sibling item Z2114 (accidental, not read further).

Ran the partial correlation on all 4703 primes p≡1(4) in [10³,10⁵] (U from a fresh full solution enumerator; residual r = log U after log log p; L(1,χ_p) by Euler product over the first 3000 primes): corr(r, log τ(p−1)) = −0.55, corr(r, σ(p−1)/(p−1)) = −0.59 (item's ±0.53 reproduced), corr(r, log L(1,χ_p)) = −0.70 (larger L ⇒ harder, the BM/T(p) direction). Partial corr of log τ(p−1) given log L: −0.22 (still significant); adding #{q∈{3,5,7,11,13,16}: q | p−1} drops it to −0.03 (σ(p−1)/(p−1): −0.05). So the τ(p−1) signal beyond L(1,χ_p) is exactly the small-modulus residue-class effect already modelled in RESIDUE_HARDNESS.md §2.2–§3 (practical/smooth p−1 '67–100 % explained', 'not about smoothness per se but divisibility by small primes'); main-term refinement only.

Did the step analytically instead of enumerating: write L = pk, d_i = L/x_i | pk with d₁+d₂+d₃ = 4k. If p ∤ k and no d_i is divisible by p then all d_i | k and Σd_i ≤ 3k < 4k; hence some d_i = p·e and k ≥ (p+2)/4 (PROVED, elementary). So no 'small multiple' L of p works (L ≥ p(p+2)/4 always), and the forced shape p·e + d₂ + d₃ = 4k with e, d₂, d₃ | k is just Elsholtz–Tao's parametrisation — e = 1, (d₂,d₃) = (u,B), k = uBC is literally (★) p + u + B = 4uBC. The 'three-divisor partition' reformulation therefore collapses to the known divisor/(★) form (FRONTIER §1–2.1); the repo has the related minlcm statistics only in z52b fingerprint items (minlcm(p)/p, Z-fingerprint #32–33).

OAI_DUMP_IMPACT.md (paragraph '023/026/027/182/279') already screens 182: its prime-argument theorem imports 003 and difference-set machinery, and 'even a valid power saving cannot apply to ES exceptions without a difference-avoidance theorem'. Doing the item's check: ES conditions are single-integer divisor/congruence events (p ≡ −(u+B) mod 4uB; d | 4Cp+1 in a class), not statements that a dense set avoids differences P(q); the exceptional set E is only closed under taking divisors (ES(d) ⇒ ES(md)), has no additive closure and density 0 (Vaughan), so no Sárközy-type statement applies. Nothing to transfer.

Wrote a full-solution enumerator recording min(y−x), min(z−y) and ran all 17 984 primes ≤ 2·10⁵: at p≡1(4) log(min(y−x))/log p has median 0.73→0.75 (q10 0.56→0.62, rising) across windows, min(y−x) ≤ log²p for 0.1% of p in [10⁴,5·10⁴) and 0 beyond 5·10⁴; min(z−y) is always ≥ p and divisible by p (median exponent 1.46). So near-isosceles gaps are ≍ p^{3/4}, never bounded or polylog — the hoped-for uniform near-degenerate family does not exist (EVIDENCE). Exact lemma (PROVED, checked on all 8956 Type I minimisers): with p ∤ x(x+g), z = pw, 4w−1 = pm, a gap-g solution ⟺ (2mg)² + (pm+1)² = s² with x = (pm+1−2mg+s)/(4m), which forces m > p/(2g²), i.e. small gaps need z ≳ p³/g².
